title: Primitive Obsession with Security Parameters
pattern: Accepting a raw string parameter representing SQL, HTML, or system commands, and relying on callers or manual code review to ensure it is sanitized.
why_bad: The security invariant exists only in developers' heads. A developer can easily pass unsanitized user input, introducing catastrophic SQL injection or XSS vulnerabilities.
detection: A database or HTML-generation method accepts raw string parameters and directly executes or interpolates them without validating them via a compile-time constant checker.
counterexample: Using a strong wrapper type like `TrustedSqlString` which can only be constructed from secure, compile-time constants.
fix: Require a wrapper type: `void execute_query(TrustedSqlString sql)` to guarantee the compile-time safety contract.
source: Heather Adkins, Building Secure and Reliable Systems, p. 252 [367, 370-371].
